reading.body:
The open-source voice and service agent space is currently represented by three active Python frameworks with a combined 39,887 GitHub stars, suggesting genuine but still concentrated developer interest rather than a fragmented or mature ecosystem.

The three repositories, pipecat, agents, and ten-framework, are closely matched in star counts, with no single project dominating. All three were pushed within hours of each other on the same day the data was generated, confirming active maintenance across the board. Each targets realtime, conversational voice AI, meaning they compete directly for the same developer audience rather than occupying distinct niches.

Realtime voice workloads place specific demands on compute and infrastructure. Low-latency inference, continuous audio streaming, and session state all require resources that are provisioned and billed differently from batch processing. These frameworks sit at the application layer and do not themselves reveal anything about the underlying power or data-center footprint their deployments consume. The data covers only repository metadata and says nothing about production usage, adoption by enterprises, or the inference providers these frameworks connect to.
